title: A network-guided protocol to discover susceptibility genes in GWAS using stability selection
author: Climente-González, Azencott, et al.

steps.title: Prepare input files
steps.instruction: Create the required input files for the pipeline. Prepare the case‑control GWAS dataset in PLINK binary format (bed, fam, bim). If the data are in PLINK text format (ped, map), convert them with `plink -file input -make-bed -out output`. Perform any necessary quality‑control steps (imputation, SNP/sample filtering, population‑structure correction) beforehand, as the pipeline does not do QC. Optionally, generate a tab‑separated gene‑gene interaction network file with columns “gene1” and “gene2”; if omitted the pipeline will query HINT8 for human protein‑protein interactions. Optionally, provide a PLINK binary reference dataset for linkage‑disequilibrium patterns (e.g., ancestry‑matched Phase 3 1000 Genomes data downloaded from the VEGAS2 offline page). Ensure the reference samples have the same ancestry as the GWAS dataset; otherwise omit this file.

substeps.instruction: Convert GWAS data to PLINK binary format if needed.
Perform QC steps outside the pipeline.
Create optional gene‑gene network file (gene1, gene2).
Create optional LD reference dataset in PLINK binary format.

steps.title: Run the pipeline command
steps.instruction: Execute the encapsulated pipeline using the single command supplied by the authors, providing the prepared GWAS binary files and any optional network or LD reference files as arguments. The command will automatically carry out all downstream analyses.

steps.title: Subsample GWAS dataset
steps.instruction: The pipeline will create five equally sized subsamples of the input GWAS dataset (default) without replacement; each subsample is processed independently.

steps.title: Chi‑squared SNP association
steps.instruction: For each subsample, compute a chi‑squared test of association between every SNP and the phenotype using PLINK 1.9.

steps.title: Compute gene‑level scores
steps.instruction: Transform the SNP‑level chi‑squared results into gene‑level association scores with VEGAS2.

steps.title: Run network‑based algorithms
steps.instruction: Apply the five network‑based methods—dmGWAS, heinz, LEAN, SConES, and SigMod—to each subsample. SConES uses SNP‑level information; the other four use the gene‑level scores generated by VEGAS2.

steps.title: Compile algorithmic solutions
steps.instruction: Collect and aggregate the gene (or SNP) selections produced by the five algorithms across all subsamples into a combined result set.

steps.title: Curate consensus subnetwork
steps.instruction: Inspect how often each gene appears in the aggregated solutions (e.g., plot a histogram). Choose a frequency threshold (such as the top 1 % most frequently selected genes). From the original gene‑gene interaction network, extract the subnetwork consisting of genes exceeding the threshold together with all edges connecting them.

substeps.instruction: Generate a histogram of gene selection frequencies.
Extract the subnetwork of selected genes and their connecting edges.

description: We have encapsulated the complex pipeline from Climente-González et al. (2021)1 into a single command (see run the pipeline and Figure 1A). The pipeline performs the following steps:Figure 1Overview of the pipeline stable_network_gwas.nf and its output(A) Visual depiction of the pipeline. The Manhattan plot comes from in Climente-González et al. (2021).1(B) Top 10 lines from the stable_consensus.tsv file applied to the data in Climente-González et al. (2021).1 Subsample the input GWAS dataset multiple times (five, by default) without replacement. Each equally sized subsample is analyzed independently, and only the final results are aggregated in the last step. The rationale is that the common part of the solutions obtained independently captures something true about the data. In contrast, the differing parts result from the sampling procedure and idiosyncrasies of the algorithm. Compute a chi-squared test of association between each SNP and the phenotype using PLINK 1.9.10 Compute a gene-level association score based on the association at the SNP level using VEGAS2.11 Use five algorithms to find important genes in a biological network: dmGWAS,2 heinz,3 LEAN,4 SConES5,12 and SigMod.6 SConES uses SNP-level information, while the rest uses gene-level information. Compile the solutions of the different methods on the multiple subsamples.
